boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten documented University of Dallas places for focused work, conversation, reflection, and campus community.

cards.title: Frassati's
cards.subtitle: Haggar University Center
cards.notes: Bring a reading assignment or laptop and use the booths, high tables, or window nooks for a focused solo session between commitments.

cards.evidence_claim: University reporting says Frassati's has grab-and-go food options and window seating used for studying.
cards.source_title: Building on Tradition: New Student-Centered Improvements Across Campus

cards.title: Cowan-Blakley Memorial Library
cards.subtitle: Campus library
cards.notes: Choose the periodicals room when you need a designated quiet zone, or move among the basement and upper-floor tables to match your task.
cards.short_summary: A multi-floor library with quiet space, tables, desks, books, and games.
cards.evidence_claim: The university study-spots guide identifies the periodicals room as a quiet zone and describes study tables and desks on multiple floors.
cards.access_notes: Library access and services may vary by academic calendar; check the library site before arrival.

cards.title: SB Hall Third Floor
cards.subtitle: Satish & Yasmin Gupta College of Business
cards.notes: Use one of the third-floor booths or tables when you want a quieter indoor setting for an individual assignment or a small work session.
cards.short_summary: A third-floor study area with booths and tables in SB Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The university guide describes SB Hall's third floor as a quiet study area with booths and tables.
cards.access_notes: Inside an academic building; building access may be limited outside normal operating periods.

cards.title: Braniff Third Floor
cards.subtitle: Braniff Graduate School of Liberal Arts
cards.notes: Set up at the circularly oriented desks for a reading group, or claim one of the nearby tables for collaborative notes and discussion.
cards.short_summary: A sunlit third-floor area arranged for shared study and conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: The university guide describes Braniff's third floor as a study spot with a sunroof, circular desks, and additional circular tables.
cards.access_notes: Inside an academic building; confirm access during evenings, weekends, and academic breaks.

cards.title: Haggerty Science Window Nooks
cards.subtitle: Haggerty Science Building, overlooking the Mall
cards.notes: Use a window nook for a short, focused block of work with an indoor view of the Mall; bring materials ready to start promptly.
cards.short_summary: Built-in indoor nooks that face the campus Mall.
cards.evidence_claim: The university guide identifies Haggerty Science Center window nooks as comfortable indoor study locations with views of the Mall.
cards.access_notes: Inside an academic building; access can depend on building schedules and university policies.

cards.title: Outside the Cap Bar
cards.subtitle: Outdoor seating beside the Cap Bar
cards.notes: Take class readings outdoors at the vine-shaded seating area, and plan a backup indoor location if weather or heat makes it impractical.
cards.short_summary: A shaded outdoor campus area beside the Cap Bar for studying and conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: The university guide describes an outdoor study area outside the Cap Bar shaded by winding vines.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space; use normal campus access rules and adjust plans for weather.

cards.title: Constantin Memorial Garden
cards.subtitle: Outside the Gorman Faculty Lounge, central Mall
cards.notes: Choose a patio seat for reading or outlining a paper, especially when you want a brief outdoor pause close to the center of campus.
cards.short_summary: A patio garden on the Mall for outdoor reading and study.
cards.evidence_claim: The university guide locates Constantin Memorial Garden outside the Gorman Faculty Lounge and describes it as an outdoor study spot.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor area near Gorman; observe campus access rules and weather conditions.

cards.title: Outside Braniff
cards.subtitle: Exterior of Braniff Graduate School of Liberal Arts
cards.notes: Use the built-in exterior benches or outdoor tables for reading, then move inside if you need power, quieter conditions, or climate control.
cards.short_summary: Outdoor benches and tables surrounding the Braniff building.
cards.evidence_claim: The university guide describes built-in wall benches and outdoor tables around Braniff as a reading location.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor seating around an academic building; access is subject to campus conditions and policies.

cards.title: Church Lawn and Amphitheater
cards.subtitle: Outside the Church of the Incarnation
cards.notes: Meet a classmate on the stone seating to review material outdoors, or use the lawn for a quiet reading break before or after campus events.

cards.evidence_claim: University news says the stone amphitheater around the Church lawn provides space to gather, study, pray, and hold outdoor lectures.

cards.short_summary: A renovated residence-hall lounge with seating, television, kitchen equipment, and ping-pong.
cards.evidence_claim: University news reports that Gregory Hall's renovated lounge has couches, a TV, and a ping-pong table for dorm-community activities.
cards.source_title: Building on Tradition: New Student-Centered Improvements Across Campus
cards.access_notes: Residential space; access is limited to residents and authorized guests under residence-life policies.

cards.access_notes: For UD students; listed Wednesdays, 8–10 p.m., in Anselm 230.

cards.access_notes: Event admission, venue rules, and business hours vary; review the specific event or business page.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented University of Dallas rituals and recurring campus practices, from the Groundhog weekend to Rome-program traditions.

cards.title: Groundhog Weekend
cards.subtitle: Annual University of Dallas celebration
cards.notes: Watch for the annual late-January or early-February schedule, then choose a daytime event such as the 5K, lecture, game, or Tower climb.
cards.short_summary: A student-built Groundhog Day celebration dating to a 1963 challenge from President Donald Cowan.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Dallas identifies Groundhog as its oldest tradition and says the annual celebration began after President Donald Cowan challenged students in 1963 to establish traditions.
cards.source_title: Communitas — Whatever We Do, We Do It With Style!
cards.access_notes: Dates and activities change annually; consult the current University of Dallas Groundhog schedule before attending.

cards.title: Wear the Groundhog “Ticket”
cards.subtitle: Groundhog Park entry tradition
cards.notes: If attending the Park event, check the current Groundhog information for its wearable-ticket requirements and pickup details before making plans.
cards.short_summary: Student-designed Groundhog shirts or sweatshirts function as the event’s distinctive entry ticket.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Dallas reports that Groundhog participants wear a student-designed T-shirt or sweatshirt for entry into Groundhog Park, with annual designs selected through student submissions.
cards.source_title: Communitas — Whatever We Do, We Do It With Style!
cards.access_notes: This practice is tied to Groundhog Park; review the current event page for eligibility, pickup, and entry information.

cards.title: Join Junior-Led Charity Week
cards.subtitle: Fall campus fundraising tradition
cards.notes: Look for the junior class’s fall schedule and support a listed booth, activity, or fundraiser connected to that year’s charitable beneficiaries.
cards.short_summary: A fall week of student-run fundraising and campus activities organized by the junior class.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Dallas describes Charity Week as a university tradition led by the junior class each fall, with student-run events, booths, and activities raising money for charity.
cards.access_notes: The beneficiary and program vary by year; use the current Charity Week schedule and organizers’ guidance.

cards.title: The Charity Week Professor “Jail”
cards.subtitle: A recurring Charity Week fundraising practice
cards.notes: Treat this as a scheduled, organizer-run Charity Week activity: check the official program for the year’s format rather than assuming a repeat.
cards.short_summary: Playful mock imprisonment of professors is part of UDallas’s description of its Charity Week observance.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Dallas says students spend a fall week practicing charity through Charity Week, including imprisoning respected professors; student media documents professor escapes as part of the practice’s history.
cards.access_notes: Only participate through the current Charity Week organizers and posted event procedures.

cards.title: Greek Olympics at Due Santi
cards.subtitle: Rome Program semester tradition
cards.notes: Students in the Rome Program can ask program staff about the semester’s Greek Olympics and any participation or travel arrangements.
cards.short_summary: A traditional set of Olympic games associated with University of Dallas’s Rome experience.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Dallas calls the Greek Olympic games a tradition in which Rome-program students participate each semester.
cards.source_title: Communitas — A Summer Like No Other: Rome Edition
cards.access_notes: This tradition belongs to the Rome Program; participation is coordinated through that program rather than the Irving campus.

cards.title: The Due Santi Vineyard Harvest
cards.subtitle: Rome Program cultural experience
cards.notes: Rome participants should ask program staff whether a harvest activity is offered during their term and follow all staff instructions for the visit.
cards.short_summary: A University of Dallas Rome-program tradition tied to participating in an Italian vineyard harvest.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Dallas identifies the vineyard harvest as one of the traditions created through its Due Santi campus experience in Rome.
cards.access_notes: Availability is program- and season-dependent; confirm details directly with Rome Program staff.

cards.title: Spring Formal
cards.subtitle: Undergraduate social tradition
cards.notes: Check Student Activities announcements near the end of spring semester for the current formal’s location, registration, dress guidance, and timing.
cards.short_summary: A named University of Dallas undergraduate tradition listed alongside Groundhog and Charity Week.
cards.evidence_claim: The University of Dallas academic catalog lists Spring Formal among undergraduate traditions organized and sponsored through Student Affairs.
cards.source_title: University of Dallas Academic Catalog — Campus Life
cards.access_notes: Event format and attendance details vary by year; follow the current Student Activities announcement.

cards.title: UDallas Oktoberfest
cards.subtitle: Fall German-themed campus tradition
cards.notes: Look for the Campus Activities Board’s current fall listing and attend the official event, which may change in format from year to year.
cards.short_summary: University of Dallas’s own glossary describes Oktoberfest as a fall tradition with food, drink, and polka music.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Dallas’s admissions glossary calls Oktoberfest its interpretation of a German classic and identifies it as a fall tradition.
cards.access_notes: Use the current Campus Activities Board event information; choose non-alcoholic options if refreshments are offered.

cards.title: Winter Concert & Carol Sing
cards.subtitle: University of Dallas Christmas-season tradition
cards.notes: Watch university music and events announcements during the Christmas season, then confirm the performance date, venue, and any attendance guidance.
cards.short_summary: A cherished campus winter music tradition highlighted by the university in its Christmas greeting.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Dallas describes its Winter Concert & Carol Sing as a cherished UDallas tradition.
cards.source_title: Communitas — A Special Christmas Greeting from the University of Dallas
cards.access_notes: Performance details vary annually; verify the current music or campus-events listing before attending.

cards.title: The Big Event: Serving Irving
cards.subtitle: Annual student-run Irving service day
cards.notes: Register through Student Activities when the annual service-day sign-up opens, then follow the assigned project’s transportation and safety instructions.
cards.short_summary: A one-day student service project through which the UDallas community thanks Irving residents.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Dallas says that since 2021, The Big Event: Serving Irving has become its largest one-day, student-run service project, bringing together students, faculty, staff, and alumni annually.
cards.access_notes: Participation is organized through Student Activities; project assignments and registration requirements vary by year.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Dallas, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure first-weekend loop through recognizable campus landmarks, student-life resources, and recurring ways to join in.

cards.title: Start at the Tower
cards.subtitle: A familiar campus meetup point
cards.notes: Use the Tower as a simple first landmark, then orient yourself toward the Mall and nearby campus buildings before choosing your next stop.
cards.short_summary: Begin with a recognizable meeting point and get your bearings.
cards.evidence_claim: UDallas identifies “Meet Us at the Tower” as a phrase students commonly use when meeting friends.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark; follow posted campus-access guidance.

cards.title: Walk the Mall
cards.subtitle: Central campus corridor near the Tower
cards.notes: Take an unhurried pass along the Mall to connect the Tower, library buildings, and gathering spaces; use it to recognize routes before classes begin.
cards.short_summary: A daylight orientation walk through a central campus area.
cards.evidence_claim: The library’s Braniff and Blakley buildings are located on the Mall, north of the Tower.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor route; use the campus map and observe posted access rules.

cards.title: Find the Cowan-Blakley Library
cards.subtitle: Braniff and Blakley Buildings on the Mall
cards.notes: Locate the Braniff Foyer entrance and save the library as a dependable study-and-research stop for your first academic week.
cards.short_summary: Identify the campus library and its entrance before coursework begins.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cowan-Blakley Memorial Library is in the Braniff and Blakley Buildings, connected by an indoor walkway.
cards.access_notes: Public hours are listed as 8 a.m.–5 p.m. Monday–Friday, with calendar-dependent variations.

cards.title: Get oriented in Haggar
cards.subtitle: Student services and gathering spaces
cards.notes: Walk through Haggar to locate Student Activities and Student Life, then note the services you may need once the first week starts moving quickly.
cards.short_summary: Pinpoint practical student-life resources in one building.
cards.evidence_claim: UDallas lists Student Activities on Haggar’s main floor and Student Life on its second floor.
cards.access_notes: Office availability varies; check the relevant office before making a special trip.

cards.title: Pause at the Church of the Incarnation
cards.subtitle: Near the center of the Irving campus
cards.notes: If reflection or worship fits your weekend, step inside respectfully and check the church page for the current Mass, confession, and event schedule.
cards.short_summary: A central campus landmark for quiet reflection or worship.
cards.evidence_claim: The Church of the Incarnation serves the university community and welcomes students, staff, faculty, and neighbors.
cards.access_notes: Check the church’s current schedule before attending a service or event.

cards.title: Notice the Reliquary Chapel
cards.subtitle: Inside the Church of the Incarnation
cards.notes: While visiting the church, look for the St. Thomas Aquinas Reliquary Chapel and treat it as a quiet, respectful stop rather than a rushed photo break.
cards.short_summary: A distinctive sacred space within the campus church.
cards.evidence_claim: UDallas states that the Church of the Incarnation includes the St. Thomas Aquinas Reliquary Chapel.
cards.access_notes: Located within an active worship space; respect services and posted guidance.

cards.title: Sit on the Church Lawn
cards.subtitle: Outside the Church of the Incarnation
cards.notes: Bring a friend or a book for a short outdoor reset, using the lawn’s seating as a calm place to pause between your campus walk and evening plans.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped outdoor gathering and reflection area.
cards.evidence_claim: UDallas describes the renovated Church Lawn as a place for contemplation, conversation, prayer, outdoor classes, and quiet moments.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space around the church; observe any event setup or posted restrictions.

cards.title: Locate the Maher Athletic Center
cards.subtitle: Home base for Crusader athletics
cards.notes: Find the athletic center now so you can recognize it on game days or when looking for campus fitness and recreation options later in the semester.
cards.short_summary: Get familiar with a major athletics and fitness destination.
cards.evidence_claim: UDallas identifies the Maher Athletic Center as housing its 15 men’s and women’s NCAA Division III varsity sports.
cards.access_notes: Athletic and fitness access may depend on student status, schedules, and facility policies.

cards.title: Catch Music on the Mall
cards.subtitle: Friday activity on the Mall
cards.notes: On a Friday, listen as students play music on the Mall; if you want to participate, use the university’s sign-up process for a DJ shift.
cards.short_summary: A recurring Friday music activity that makes the Mall feel lived-in.
cards.evidence_claim: CAB says students play music on the Mall every Friday from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. and can sign up for DJ shifts.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists Fridays, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; confirm programming for the particular academic-weekend date.

cards.title: Check out Rec Programming
cards.subtitle: Student-organized recreation and intramurals
cards.notes: Browse current recreation options and choose one low-stakes way to join in, such as a class, tournament, or intramural activity that fits your comfort level.
cards.short_summary: A practical route into student-organized recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: UDallas Rec Programming includes recreational classes, weekend and one-day tournaments, and intramural sports organized by students.
cards.access_notes: Participation is for current UD students, faculty, or staff and requires a Student Activities General Waiver before registration.
